samples.text:
The chart gives the information about the percentage of workers who work in agriculture, industry and services in Vietnam, Mexico, Poland and Canada in 2022.

In Vietnam, the three sectors are quite similar. Services is 37%, agriculture is 33% and industry is 30%. So the workers is divided almost equally. Vietnam also has the highest agriculture of all four countries.

In Mexico and Poland, services is much more bigger than the other sectors. Mexico has 62% in services, 26% in industry and 12% in agriculture. Poland is similar with 60% in services, but industry is higher at 32%, which is the highest percentage for industry. Agriculture in Poland is only 8%.

Canada has the most workers in services, it is 79%. Industry is 19% and agriculture is only 2%, which is the lowest figure in the chart.

Overall, services was the biggest sector in every country, while agriculture was small in all countries except Vietnam, where it was nearly one third of the workers.
samples.why: Figures accurate and all countries described · simple overview at the end · repetitive structures and linking · some inaccurate word choice · several agreement, comparative and tense errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart illustrates the proportion of the workforce employed in three economic sectors, namely agriculture, industry and services, in four countries in 2022.

Overall, the service sector was the largest employer in all four countries, although its dominance varied considerably. Vietnam had a much more even distribution of workers than the other countries, while agriculture accounted for only a small share of jobs in Mexico, Poland and Canada.

In Vietnam, employment was split fairly evenly, with 37% of workers in services, 33% in agriculture and 30% in industry. Its agricultural figure was far higher than those of the other nations, being almost three times that of Mexico (12%).

Mexico and Poland had very similar profiles, with services employing 62% and 60% of their workforces respectively. However, industry was slightly more significant in Poland, where it accounted for 32%, the highest figure for this sector, compared to 26% in Mexico. Canada was the most service-oriented economy, with almost four-fifths of workers (79%) in this sector. Only 19% of Canadians worked in industry, and just 2% was employed in agriculture, the lowest proportion recorded.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main pattern · key features highlighted with apt comparisons · logical paragraphing and a range of linkers · some less common vocabulary · mostly accurate grammar with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The chart compares the distribution of employment across agriculture, industry and services in Vietnam, Mexico, Poland and Canada in 2022.

In every country, services provided the largest share of jobs, but the extent of this varied markedly. Vietnam stood apart as the only country with a substantial agricultural workforce and a roughly even three-way split, whereas Canada's economy was overwhelmingly service-based.

Vietnam's workers were distributed almost equally between the three sectors: 37% were in services, 33% in agriculture and 30% in industry. Its agricultural share was nearly three times that of Mexico and more than sixteen times that of Canada.

Mexico and Poland occupied the middle ground, with services employing around three-fifths of workers in each (62% and 60% respectively). The two differed mainly in the balance between the other sectors: Poland had the largest industrial workforce of the four countries, at 32%, and only 8% in agriculture, while Mexico's figures were 26% and 12%.

At the other extreme, Canada had 79% of its workforce in services, the highest proportion shown, leaving just 19% in industry and a negligible 2% in agriculture.
samples.why: Well-chosen key features and a clear overview · accurate figures and derived comparisons · skilful organisation from most balanced to most service-based · precise vocabulary · wide range of error-free structures.
